content:
**readers report the collapse (#634)**

#598 changed the shared reader from one-per-physical-line to one-per-id. The number is right and it fixed a real leak, but six consumers read through it, all their totals moved on one commit, and none could say why: brain:metrics printed 13/2046 while the store held 2185 lines. Ruled: report at the readers that PRINT a count, stay silent at the readers that only TEST existence -- and PROVE the silence rather than assert it. memoryPresence is obs.some(o => o?.type === 'session_summary') and dedup is first-wins, so the predicate is invariant under dedup for ANY predicate; verified by a test that asserts both preconditions (the reader really collapsed, there really were repeats) so it cannot pass against a fixture that never had duplicates. The register of who reads what lives at readRecordObservations, the one chokepoint all six share, carrying the RULE for the next consumer rather than just the list. The reviewer's cold boot stays silent as a recorded ruling: a verdict is about a pull request, while store hygiene is a merge=union residual from unrelated branches that the PR author cannot act on -- and deduping there is required, or a doctrine record gets weighed twice. Found while implementing: renderJson denormalizes the coverage snapshot onto EVERY period row, so passing duplicates.groups through measured 6871 bytes per row against 111, 62x, about 79 KiB of repetition on a twelve-period run; projected to counts explicitly (not by delete) and without mutating the caller's object, since both renderers read the same snapshot. share() on a store-less repo materializes an empty .memory/index.jsonl: documented rather than gated, because gating would change #246's contract to fix a misreading nothing makes -- computeMemoryCoverage resolves store presence from existsSync(records/), never from the index. Also recorded: the PR template describes an issue-scoped memory-gate that does not exist in the code.
